messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] HIGH ERROR RATE detected in corpx-vpc -> dedicated pool corpx-prod-pool-7 - error rate 37% over last 5m, 502/500-series spike. Autoretry thresholds tripped.

layla (oncall): acked. I'm on it, pulling logs and KV cache stats.

tayla (oncall): initial impact: ~12 tenants with elevated 5xx, corpx (tenant: corpX) is highest - about 45% of errors. Latency up for short requests too.

ram (sre): pinging ana and sam. Is this likely a model OOM or infra networking? Any spikes on GPU util?

ana (eng-runtime): looking at host metrics - GPU mem stable, kernel OOM counters low. KV cache eviction up for corpx workload. Could be cache churn due to long-tail prompts.

sam (eng-ops): checking LB and VPC logs now. I see a flurry of TCP resets from 10.43.78.0/24 into the pool - suspect a misbehaving tenant client causing request storms.

matt (acct-mgr): corpX is on an enterprise Dedicated plan (corpX-prod-pool-7). They currently have live traffic. I'm opening a support bridge with them now. @jess can you join customer call?

jess (cust-success): on the line with corpX now, they confirm a recent client-side deploy that increased concurrency. They want mitigation asap.

tayla (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) isolate corpX traffic off prod pool to a newly provisioned dedicated lane (temp) 2) enable per-tenant rate limiting for corpX 3) if pool still degrades, failover corpX to hosted fallback model (with Egress consent) 4) collect full traces + QPS profiles.

ana (eng-runtime): I can push a canary route to divert corpX requests to corpx-pool-temp-1. Command:

```bash
# apply tenant route
redwoodctl route add --tenant corpx --pool corpx-pool-temp-1 --priority 10
```

sam (eng-ops): provisioning temp pool now (g4dn x2). ETA ~6m. I'll also apply iptables backpressure to reduce connection bursts: 

```bash
# limit new connections per src
sudo iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m connlimit --connlimit-above 200 -j REJECT
```

tayla (oncall): applying per-tenant rate limit in config:

```json
{"tenant":"corpx","max_concurrency":40,"burst":10}
```

ops-bot: corpX temp pool creation started (job id: 99a1). Estimated 5 mins.

ram (sre): Tayla, Ana - when corpX is on temp pool, please monitor error rate and KV cache hit ratio. If drop <5% in 2m, consider full switch.

ana (eng-runtime): corpX route applied to corpx-pool-temp-1. Monitoring.

jess (cust-success): corpX on phone: they see partial recovery already. They're asking for an ETA to return to normal and what root cause will look like.

tayla (oncall): short answer to corpX: we've isolated your traffic to a temporary pool and applied rate limiting. We expect stabilized service in ~10-15m. We'll follow up with RCA and any credits if SLA breached.

matt (acct-mgr): noted. I'll prep an interim note to their CTO. Draft:

"We're actively mitigating a traffic surge originating from your recent deploy. We've isolated your traffic and applied protective limits. We'll follow up with a timeline and RCA."

zara (security): quick note - verify KMS rotations and HSM logs while migrating traffic. No sign of exfil but want to be safe.

sam (eng-ops): temp pool healthy. error rate for corpX down from 45% -> 6% within 4m. KV hit ratio improving.

tayla (oncall): good. I'll keep monitoring. Next steps: collect full traffic traces (5m window), grab heap/dmesg from pool nodes, and draft RCA skeleton.

ana (eng-runtime): collecting traces and will attach anonymized spans. Also running quick diff on model versions serving corpX to ensure no incompatible variant was rolled.

ops-bot: job 99a1 completed - pool corpx-pool-temp-1 ready.

ram (sre): handoff in 30m to ram for postmortem and customer follow-up. Tayla, leave notes in incident doc: mitigation timeline, commands run, decision to route.

tayla (oncall): adding notes to incident doc: applied iptables connlimit, created corpx-pool-temp-1, applied tenant rate-limits, diverted traffic at 1768901340.

jess (cust-success): corpX happy with immediate mitigation. Requesting a formal post-incident write-up + timeline and confirmation of any SLA credit. Can we commit to a 48h RCA delivery?

matt (acct-mgr): agree to 48h RCA. Also propose a joint CTI call with corpX execs tomorrow at 14:00 PT. I'll coordinate.

ram (sre): taking over for RCA. I'll draft root cause (prelim): high client concurrency from customer deploy caused KV cache churn + connection storms; autoscaling lag and per-tenant concurrency not enforced on older pool. Mitigations: tenant isolation, per-tenant rate limiting, new autoscale policy. Action items: 1) full RCA doc within 48h 2) permanent routing to dedicated pool with stronger per-tenant quotas 3) add alert for KV eviction spike 4) SOC check (zara)

zara (security): acknowledged. I'll run integrity checks and confirm no suspicious auth events. Report in 4h.

ana (eng-runtime): follow-up: discovered older model variant (v2.1) on corpx-prod-pool-7 that handles KV differently -> higher cache thrash for certain prompt patterns. Will include in RCA.

tayla (oncall): last note before handoff: incident declared mitigated at 1768901500. Errors back to baseline ~1.2%. Handing to @ram for postmortem and customer comms. Thanks team :tada:

ram (sre): thanks. I'll draft RCA and a short exec summary for internal and for corpX. Matt/Jess I'll loop you in on the external draft. Also will propose a one-time SLA credit calculation (pro-rated for 2.8h of impact) and include in the external comms.

jess (cust-success): will coordinate customer-sent acknowledgement once external note is finalized. Scheduling follow-up meeting invite now.

matt (acct-mgr): sending interim email to corpX CTO now. Copying in ops notes.

incident-bot: incident CLOSED (mitigated). Timeline and artifacts saved to incident-doc://1768901234

ram (sre): placeholder for RCA link: https://redwood-internal/incident/1768901234/rca (draft). Please comment.

ana (eng-runtime): uploading trace tarball and model diffs to the incident doc.

jess (cust-success): once RCA final, I'll include exec-friendly summary: root cause, mitigation, remediation, SLA credit, next steps.

tayla (oncall): closing out on-call. leaving detailed runbook note: if similar KV eviction spike occurs -> immediate tenant diversion + temp pool + reduce concurrency.

matt (acct-mgr): thanks everyone. Good triage.
